Fixed: valve_state is now persisted to config/valve_state.json on every set_valve call and reloaded at Supervisor init (falls back to False for unknown valves). Restore only updates the in-memory model - never writes to hardware, keeping connect/restart read-only. Verified with a two-Supervisor repro (simulated restart): state survives, and the restore step made zero hardware writes. Superseded and REMOVED the same day it shipped. The restart re-exec'd the process; on 2026-08-25 an old instance survived it, so two servers ran at once - the newer holding port 8000 while the older still held COM8-COM12 - and every device looked unreachable. Zach: 'I don't need a restart, really, just a button that kills all servers in use.' Replaced by Diagnostics > Shut down server, which kills sibling reactor processes first, then tears itself down through the normal lifespan teardown and calls os._exit(0). See reactor-tp1/reactor-799 notes and docs/CONTROL_MODEL.md. KEY LESSON KEPT: main() returning does NOT end the process - a non-daemon thread keeps it alive, which is exactly how that orphan survived holding its serial ports.

Supervisor.stop() now calls abort_prestart() when a pre-start is running OR has completed and left the tool primed - the primed case counts because a successful pre-start deliberately leaves Ar flowing, the fill pulsing, the relay set, HV up and the DC supplies on, and a shutdown would otherwise abandon all of it. Implemented. Step gains bias_v/bias_polarity/bias_lead_s/bias_trail_s, set only by build_ald_recipe/build_cvd_recipe when the run's Sample bias is non-zero. RecipeRunner._schedule_bias queues each flip as its own task (newest instruction supersedes any pending flip due at or after it), so the lead runs down inside pump A and the trail inside pump B and a cycle still takes the sum of its step durations. EE-CVD awaits the lead/trail in setup/teardown instead. Supervisor.set_sample_bias_output does the switching, writing the level only on the first ON of a run. supplies_output_on now ARMS the bias at pre-start (level+polarity, output off). UI: Bias lead/trail in Advanced timing, hints and the pre-start dialog reworded. tests/test_sample_bias_bracket.py added (timings, no reignite cycling, no cycle lengthening, abort, EE-CVD); test_keithley_supplies updated for arm-not-on. Fixed in three layers. (1) Supervisor.stop() now runs every step through _teardown(): each is bounded (3-8s) and logged by name, and the loop-task cancels use asyncio.wait with a timeout because a to_thread DAQ read cannot be cancelled once its thread starts. (2) reactor/__main__.py arms a 20s hard-deadline daemon thread when shutdown is requested, so the process ends and releases the DAQ and the COM ports even if the teardown overruns - the graceful path is the ONLY exit for this instance, since the taskkill sweep skips self and parent and the parent is the venv pythonw shim that re-exec'd us. (3) The UI polls /api/state after the POST and, if the server is still answering past the deadline, re-enables the button and says so in red with where to look - it used to grey out and lie. tests/test_shutdown_teardown.py wedges one MFC, one instrument and one supply and asserts stop() still completes (9s) with the DAQ released; without the fix it hangs forever.
